confidence_notes: I based the food and drink anchors on one web search. It returned crowdsourced cost-of-living figures from Numbeo, Expatistan, CityCost and Worksploring. Their typical prices were about INR 140-165 for a domestic draft beer, INR 100-185 for a cappuccino, INR 200-220 for an inexpensive meal and INR 800-990 for a mid-range meal for two. I converted these to USD at roughly INR 88 per USD, and that rate is my own approximation. I also adjusted the figures slightly for the July 2026 pricing window. Several sources have few data points, so the drinks figures are rough. I did not search directly for cocktail or wine prices. Those are estimates scaled from local beer prices and India's high taxes on spirits and wine. Amritsar is a religious city and alcohol is mostly sold in hotel bars and a limited number of licensed venues, so cocktail and wine prices are less certain. The accommodation anchors are general-knowledge estimates only. I did not check any booking sites or listings. The RBA rate was reported in a search-result summary for 18 November 2026; I did not open the RBA page myself.
comparable_city_reasoning: Compared with mid-sized North Indian tourist and pilgrimage cities such as Jaipur, Varanasi and Chandigarh. Accommodation reflects Amritsar's large supply of budget guesthouses and hostels near the Golden Temple, plus a mid-range hotel market.
